subject: Discovery recap: p95 latency targets, streaming UX & concurrency requirements
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@finly.com>, Maya Lopez <maya.lopez@finly.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-22T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Discovery recap: p95 latency targets, streaming UX & concurrency requirements

Thanks for the time earlier, Samir and Maya — great conversation. Below is a short recap from our call + next steps so we’re all aligned. I captured the things that matter most for your engineering and product teams.

High-level pain points
- Streaming UX is perceived as jittery for multi-turn flows; users drop after ~6–8 turns.
- Intermittent spikes in response time during heavy day-of-month batch runs.
- Current stack is a hybrid: in-house orchestration + managed model hosting for some workloads — no uniform routing or KV caching today.

Targets / success criteria you shared
- P95 latency goal (streaming first-byte) for conversational UI: <= 400ms across typical sessions (target 350ms if feasible).
- Sustained concurrency target: 800 concurrent streaming users (~200 QPS sustained; peak bursts to ~1.2k concurrent).
- Cold-start / first-token target: <150ms for streamed responses (important for perceived snappiness).
- End-to-end reliability: <=1% error rate for inference at peak.

Key constraints we heard
- Tight cost sensitivity; you prefer a predictable commit model if it reduces unit cost.
- Data residency: prod traffic routes from US regions only.
- SOC2 + security evidence required before any production contract.

What we observed (from what you shared)
- Current p95 measurements (approx): 600–900ms for streaming first-byte under medium load.
- Concurrency tests are currently limited by a single orchestration cluster; no prefix/KV caching used.

Suggested next steps (agreed on call)
1) Finly to send: 7-day traffic profile, representative request/response sizes, and current p95 logs (we’ll use this to simulate expected latency).
2) Redwood to validate: run a short PoC using a dedicated pool (config: streaming-optimized model, prefix cache enabled, batching tuned for median sequence lengths). Goal: show p95 improvement and stable concurrency to 800+.
3) Security/compliance: we’ll provide SOC2 artifacts and an evidence checklist (Connor will own this on our side).
4) Tech deep-dive workshop (60–90m): proposed slot Thu 2026-11-25 10:00–11:30 PST — engineering + infra folks.

Attachments: finly_discovery_notes.pdf (stub) — contains the summary of metrics and the sketches we discussed.

If that aligns, I’ll open a HubSpot record and we’ll schedule the workshop. Thanks again — excited to dig in.

—
Aditya Rao
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123

On Mon, Nov 22, 2026 at 14:10 Samir Patel <samir.patel@finly.com> wrote:
> Thanks Aditya — appreciate the fast follow. I’ll pull together the 7-day profile and the p95 logs for the production cluster.
> 
> Couple of clarifications from our side:
> - The 800 concurrent number is for active streaming sessions (lots of long-lived websockets). We measured ~180 QPS on weekdays but see spikes during batch closing.
> - We do have an internal caching layer but it’s not prefix-aware and doesn’t persist KV across model invocations.
> 
> We’ll aim to get the logs to you by EOD Wednesday. Please include SOC2 evidence checklist; procurement will need it before we can sign an NDA.
> 
> —Samir

From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@finly.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Maya Lopez <maya.lopez@finly.com>
Date: 2026-11-22T15:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: p95 latency targets, streaming UX & concurrency requirements

Thanks for the thorough recap, Aditya — this matches what we discussed. A couple of notes / additions:

- We measure user-perceived latency differently (client-side + network) — our backend p95s are about 420–650ms today depending on model/sequence length. We’ll include both client & server-side traces.
- For the PoC, we’ll want to test with our longest typical session (avg 1.8k tokens/session) in addition to the short-chat path.
- Procurement note: we’ll need SOC2 artifacts and an initial SOW template to start internal review.

Maya and I are available for the Thu 11/25 workshop — confirmed. I’ll upload logs to the shared Drive link you suggested and will CC procurement once we have the SOC2 checklist.

Appreciate the clear next steps. Look forward to the workshop.

—Samir
